relevance_note: Case report of a family with LCAT deficiency diagnosed clinically: "the proband was diagnosed to have classic FLD while his mother and sister were diagnosed to have FED"; no genetic testing was done.
method_note: Hand-built with a short Python script from my reading; no tables in the paper (Table 1 content is absent from the Markdown). No variant rows: the paper states genetic testing was not done ("Genetic testing of the proband ... could not be done due to financial constraints") and prints no LCAT variant; the shared mutation is only presumed ("probably having the same mutation"). Diagnoses are clinical (proband also with undetectable plasma cholesterol esterification rate). The proband is labelled 'patient' (rule 5; the paper reports one index patient and calls him 'the proband'/'our patient'); relatives 'mother of patient' and 'sister of patient' (the text says 'younger sister' once and 'sister' elsewhere). 'No renal, hematological or other systemic involvement' for the mother and sister was recorded as excluded at the level named, per D-27; it does not exclude specific checklist items (anemia, proteinuria, etc.), which stay not reported. Proteinuria not marked for the proband because only 'nephrotic syndrome' is stated. Kidney histology details partly come from the Figure 2 legend, which describes the proband's biopsy. Two previously published persons with individual-level facts were included: ref [5] patient (the one of two Indian siblings from Muthusethupathi et al. who developed ESRD requiring renal transplant; the other sibling has only a diagnosis and was left out) and ref [13] patient (Frasca et al., foam cell deposition on third kidney biopsy). The Frasca reference title in the reference list ('A 33-year-old man') was not used. n_patients_reported left null because no patient has a reported LCAT variant and the authors give no count. Age 37 recorded as age at last evaluation (age at presentation); no age at diagnosis stated. No contradictions found.
